questions.explanation: Journals are serials valued for the currency of their content, which is why recent original research and observations are published in them. Option C (textbooks) summarise established knowledge rather than report new findings, and A and B (tables, translations) are not publication types for original research.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Another word for data is......................
questions.explanation: Data means facts, or facts, figures or instructions in a form that can be processed, so another word for data is fact. Option A (information) is tempting, but information is data that has been processed to improve the user's knowledge, so the two are not the same. Option D (opinion) is a personal view, not raw facts.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Faculty handbook is an example of small ready reference source
questions.explanation: The statement is true: a handbook is a small ready reference source that gives facts on places, techniques, institutions and subjects, and Faculty and Departmental Handbooks are standard examples. Options A, C and D all deny or partly deny that.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: The following are characteristics of information except .........
questions.explanation: The characteristics of good information are availability or accessibility, accuracy, reliability, timeliness and relevance. News is one form that information can take, not a quality it has, so B is the exception, while A, C and D are all characteristics.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Information can be in form of ................
questions.explanation: Information can take many forms: oral, textual, numeric, bibliographic, graphical (graphs and charts) and multimedia. Since numbers (A), graphs and charts (C) and texts (D) are all valid forms, the right answer is B, all of them. Picking any one alone leaves out the others.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Where information is not provided on time for the purpose for which it is required, it becomes ........
questions.explanation: Timeliness is a quality of good information: it must be provided on time for the purpose it is needed for. If it comes late, it becomes irrelevant, so D is correct. Options A, B and C all describe good information, which is the opposite of what late information turns into.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Multimedia information pertains to the use of diversified medium of communication such as
questions.explanation: Multimedia information uses a mix of media of communication such as audio, visual and audio-visual, so C is correct. Text, graphs and numbers (A, B and D) are each a single type of information, textual, graphical and numeric, rather than a mix of media.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: An ............. is a summary of a publication or article
questions.explanation: An abstract is a summary of a publication or article that gives enough bibliographic detail to trace the original. Option D (index) only points to where information can be found, B (anthology) is a collection of writings, and C (atlas) is a book of maps.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Notable reference collection includes all of these EXCEPT......................
questions.explanation: General books are not part of the reference collection, because reference materials are not read from cover to cover the way books are. Notable reference collections include dictionaries, encyclopaedias, fact sources, biographies, indexes and abstracts, so A, B and D are all included and C is the exception.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: .................. is not a type of dictionary
questions.explanation: The three types of dictionary are general dictionaries, specialised dictionaries and subject dictionaries. There is no such thing as an anthem dictionary, so B is the one that is not a type, while A, C and D are all real types.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Enquiries on how to access any of the resources in a library can be made at the ........... Section
questions.explanation: Enquiries on how to access any of the library's resources are made at the Readers' Services point, so D is correct. Option B is a building, not a service point, and A (Reference) and C (Serials) are collections rather than the enquiry desk.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Biographical sources are reference materials that provide individual information such as .....
questions.explanation: Biographical sources give information on individuals such as date of birth, place of birth, education and career. Since B, C and D are all things they provide, A (all of these) is the complete answer, and picking one alone leaves out the others.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Africana collection is found in ...............
questions.explanation: At the University of Lagos Library, the Africana collection is housed in the Research and Bibliographic Department, known as the Gandhi Library, in the basement of the main library. Options C and D are separate collections on the ground floor, and A (Serials) is the collection of journals and periodicals.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Which of the following is not a secondary source of information?
questions.explanation: A thesis is a primary source: it is original research produced by the researcher and counts as grey literature. Textbooks, encyclopaedias and digests (B, C and A) compile, explain or review other people's work, which makes them secondary sources, so D is the one that is not secondary.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Electronic resources allows for ............ usage of resources at the same time
questions.explanation: Electronic (non-print) resources allow multiple people to use the same material at the same time, unlike a printed book that only one person can hold at once, so A is correct. Option C (single) describes how a print copy is used, and B and D do not describe this feature.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: The biographical source 'International Who's Who' is an example of a/an ....... source.
questions.explanation: International Who's Who is a universal and current biographical source, because it covers notable people from all over the world and is kept up to date. Options A and D describe sources limited to one country, such as Africa Who's Who or Newswatch Who's Who. Option C, 'international and local', is not a category used for biographical sources.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Directories, handbooks, yearbooks and almanacs are ............. sources
questions.explanation: Directories, handbooks, yearbooks and almanacs are fact sources: reference materials that give facts on a wide range of current issues. Option B refers to lists of books and articles on a subject, and C covers maps, atlases and gazetteers, so neither matches these four.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Reference materials contain facts and rarely contain opinions.
questions.explanation: The statement is true: reference materials mainly contain facts and rarely contain opinions, which is why we consult them for specific information instead of reading them from cover to cover. That rules out False (B) and the hedged options C and D.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: An index serves as .............. to required information
questions.explanation: An index serves as both an indicator and a pointer to required information, giving a systematic guide to the contents of a book or text, so C is the complete answer. Options A and B each capture only half of the definition, which is why C is the best choice.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: University of Lagos Library has ..................library resources
questions.explanation: The University of Lagos Library has three categories of resources: print, non-print and audio-visual. Since all three are present, 'All of these' (A) is correct. Options B, C and D each name only one category, so each is incomplete on its own.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: The following are categories of resources in the library except .........
questions.explanation: The print collections of the University of Lagos Library are Africana, Reference, Reserved, Serials and Recent accessions. There is no American collection, so C is the odd one out, while A, B and D are genuine categories.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Ability to locate, retrieve and evaluate information is known as.........
questions.explanation: Information literacy is the ability to locate, retrieve, evaluate and apply information, and to recognise when information is needed, so C is correct. Information discovery (D) sounds close but covers only finding information, not evaluating and using it. Options A and B are not terms used for this skill.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: ................. provide information on places and physical features
questions.explanation: Geographical sources provide information on places such as towns and countries and on physical features such as mountains and rivers; examples are maps, atlases, gazetteers and travel guides. Bibliographical sources (A) list books and articles, and fact sources (C) give facts on current issues, so neither deals with places and physical features.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: "Map of Nigeria" and "Travel guide" are examples of ..................
questions.explanation: Maps such as the Map of Nigeria, atlases, gazetteers and travel guides are geographical sources, which give information on places and physical features (D). Option B, fact sources, covers directories, handbooks, yearbooks and almanacs, not places. Biographical sources (A) are about people, and a bibliography (C) is a list of publications.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Collections published on Africa or African authors can be found in the University Library at the ........section
questions.explanation: Africana collections are print materials published on Africa by African and non-African authors, housed in the Research and Bibliographic Department (Gandhi Library), so A is correct. The reserved collection (B) holds rare and valuable materials across disciplines, serials (C) are periodicals, and the reference collection (D) holds dictionaries, encyclopedias and similar tools.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: A Closed Access System of collection in a library refers to ...............

options.b: Materials to be borrowed for home use
options.c: Materials to be retrieved directly by the user

questions.explanation: In a closed access system, users may not take materials from the shelves themselves; the desk officer fetches the material once the bibliographic details are given, so access is restricted (A). Option C describes the opposite, open access, and B and D are about borrowing and copying rules, not about how materials are accessed.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Fact sources at the University of lagos Library are housed at the ..........
questions.explanation: Fact sources such as directories, handbooks, yearbooks and almanacs are reference materials, so they are housed at the reference section of the library (C). The MTN Connect Library (A) and the Automation Section (D) deal with electronic, non-print resources, and the Boulos Library (B) is not where fact sources are kept.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Types of libraries include all of these EXCEPT ..................
questions.explanation: Public, academic and special libraries, along with school and private libraries, are types of library. Reserved (C) is not a type of library but a collection within a library, holding valuable and rare materials on closed access. A law or court library, for example, is a kind of special library (B).

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Reserved collections in University of lagos Library are run on ............. access system
questions.explanation: Reserved collections run on a closed access system: a user requests an item by giving its bibliographic details, and the material is fetched and used within the reading room (A). Open access (B) and self-service (C) would let users take materials from the shelves themselves, which is not allowed for reserved items. 'Reserve' (D) is the name of the collection, not the access system.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: University of lagos Library has newspapers dating as far back as .........
questions.explanation: The Gandhi Library holds newspapers, old and current, dated as far back as 1930, including the West African Pilot, so C is correct. Options A, B and D give other dates: 1860 (A) is far too early, and 1960 (D) would leave out the pre-independence papers the library holds.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Electronic journals, electronic images, library software, CD-ROMS are ................
questions.explanation: Electronic books, electronic journals, electronic images, library software and CD-ROMs are non-print resources, managed by the Automation Section and accessed in the E-Library (A). Audio-visual resources (C) refer to aids like projectors, televisions and tape recorders, and B and D wrongly include print materials.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Libraries perform all of these functions EXCEPT .....................
questions.explanation: All libraries perform the basic functions of selection, acquisition, organisation, preservation and dissemination of information resources. Book selling is a commercial activity, not a library function, so C is the odd one out, while A, B and D are all library functions.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Which of the following are types of index?

options.a: Book index, periodical index and newspaper index

questions.explanation: Indexes are pointers to published information, and they include the book index, the index to collections, the periodical index and the newspaper index (A). Option B is tempting, but indicative, informative and evaluative are the types of abstract, not index. General, specialised and subject (C) are types of dictionary, and primary and secondary (D) are sources of information.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Yearbooks are also known as ........
questions.explanation: Yearbooks are published once a year to record the facts and events of that year, which is why they are also called annuals (A). Handbooks and directories (C and D) are separate kinds of fact source alongside yearbooks, not other names for them, and a dictionary (B) deals with words, not yearly facts.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: An index serves as .............. to required information
questions.explanation: An index is a directional aid that points to and indicates where information can be found, so it serves as a pointer and indicator (B). It does not give the full text of the material (A), and a brief summary of a document (D) is an abstract, not an index.

questions.topic: Understanding the Library and Information Resources
questions.question: Dictionaries are used as quick ------- sources in the library
questions.explanation: Dictionaries are reference materials, consulted quickly for specific information such as spelling, meaning and pronunciation, and housed at the reference section of the library (D). Serial (C) refers to publications issued in successive parts, like journals and newspapers, and publication and manual (A and B) are not the category dictionaries belong to.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: The system of classification in the University of Lagos main library is
questions.explanation: The University of Lagos main library organizes its items using the Library of Congress (LC) classification scheme, so C is correct. LC uses letters A to Z for the main classes with numbers added. Option B, the Dewey Decimal system, is a different scheme, while a call mark (A) and the card catalogue (D) are tools for locating books, not classification systems.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: One of the following is not part of the card catalogue in library
questions.explanation: The manual card catalogue is arranged by author, title and subject, so author cards (B), subject cards (C) and title cards (D) are all part of it. An index card (option A) is not a type of catalogue card, which makes it the odd one out and the correct answer.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: The Dewey Decimal classification system assigns numbers in the following manner
questions.explanation: The Dewey Decimal system divides all knowledge into ten main classes numbered from 000 to 999, so D is correct, with 000 for general works up to 900 for history and geography. Options A, B and C give ranges that stop short of the full three-digit span. Note that the UNILAG main library uses the Library of Congress scheme rather than Dewey.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: In the library of congress classification system, law and languages take the following letters
questions.explanation: In the Library of Congress system, K stands for Law and P for Language and Linguistics, so law and languages take K and P, option C. Option B is wrong because L is the class for Education, not Law, and options A and D wrongly include A, which is the class for General Works.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: An --------- summarizes the accurate content and presentation of a document
questions.explanation: An abstract, option A, is a brief summary of the contents of a book, article, thesis or conference paper that tells the user what the document contains without reading it from beginning to end. An index (C) only points to where information can be found, an electronic source (B) is a format rather than a summary, and advanced search (D) is a searching technique.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Mixed notation refers to the use of letters of the alphabet as well as .............
questions.explanation: Mixed notation means combining letters of the alphabet with Arabic numerals (0 to 9), as the Library of Congress classification does, which is why it is called alpha-numeric. So C is correct. Roman numerals (B) and Greek symbols (D) are not used in this scheme, and Arabic alphabets (A) is a confusion, since the scheme uses the ordinary letters A to Z.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Letter T is assigned to books on .......... in the Library of Congress Classification Scheme
questions.explanation: In the Library of Congress scheme, the letter T is assigned to Technology, option B. Arts come under N (Fine Art), Science under Q and Medicine under R, so options A, C and D are wrong.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Arrangement in the library catalogue is in \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ order
questions.explanation: A library catalogue is arranged by author, title and subject, and its entries are filed in alphabetical order so users can look up a name or heading quickly, which is option C. Chronological order (A) would arrange by date, which is not how catalogues work. Triangular (B) is not an arrangement at all, and decimal (D) refers to a classification scheme for shelving, not the catalogue.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Information can be evaluated using the following criteria EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Information is evaluated using criteria such as currency, relevancy, authority, accuracy and purpose. Size (option C) is not one of them, since a long book or article is not more credible just because it is bigger. Accuracy (A), relevancy (B) and currency (D) are all genuine evaluation criteria.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Arrangement of materials on the shelves is done using\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
questions.explanation: Materials on the shelves are arranged using a classification scheme, option C. The University of Lagos main library uses the Library of Congress Classification Scheme (and the National Library of Medicine scheme at the College of Medicine), so books are shelved by their classification call numbers. A catalogue (A) is tempting, but it is the tool you search to find the call number, not the system that arranges the shelves. Options B and D are not library tools.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Criteria to evaluate credibility of Information resources are; currency, authority, ...... and ......
questions.explanation: The criteria for judging information resources are currency, relevancy, authority, accuracy and purpose. With currency and authority already given, the missing two are relevancy and accuracy, so C is correct. Option A pairs relevancy with intelligence and B pairs accuracy with strategy, and neither of those is a criterion. D is wrong because a correct pair is listed.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: A library's entire holding is held in a manual database called --------
questions.explanation: The library catalogue is the index and essential tool for retrieving library resources, and it gives access to everything the library holds. It exists as a manual card catalogue and as the Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC). Options A and B (book box, check list) are not library tools, and C (library holdings) is just the name for the collection itself, not the database that records it.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: One of the major benefits of using library databases is ............

options.b: That they are subscribed to by the library to support students' assignments and research
options.d: The value you get for your money

questions.explanation: A major benefit of library databases is that they are designed by publishers or aggregators and subscribed to by the library to support student assignments and research, and they are more organised and easier to cite than general web results. Options A and D (internet speed, value for money) are not benefits of this kind, and C cannot be right since those two are wrong.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Ranking of articles retrieved from databases is by ...........

options.a: No of times the search was conducted

questions.explanation: Databases mostly rank results chronologically by date, with the most recent records first, and by relevancy, based on how often and how prominently the search terms appear in a record. Options A (number of times the search was run) and C (number of records) are not ranking methods, so B (all of the above) is also wrong.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Which of these letters of the alphabet cannot be found in the Library of Congress Classification Scheme?
questions.explanation: In the Library of Congress scheme, main classes are given letters of the alphabet, but O, X and Y are reserved for future expansion, so there is no Class O. Options A, B and C are all used: G is Geography and Anthropology, S is Agriculture and C is History.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: The various tools for accessing information are called ...............
questions.explanation: The tools used to access information, such as library catalogues, the OPAC, indexes, abstracts and bibliographies, are called information retrieval tools. Options A, B and C (information guides, keys and banks) are not the terms used for these tools.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Law books in the University of Lagos Library can be found in.............
questions.explanation: Law books in the University of Lagos Library are found in Class K, because K is the Law class in the Library of Congress scheme the library uses. Options A, C and D are other classes: H is Social Science, G is Geography and Anthropology, and M is Music.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: UNILAG students have remote access to UNILAG Library online resources via
questions.explanation: UNILAG students reach the library's databases and e-resources through the UNILAG Library website, using a password for some fee-based databases when connecting from outside the campus network. A matric number, the telephone directory and a hall of residence (A, B and C) are not gateways to the online resources.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: The URL of a website accredited to a post-secondary institution or institution of higher learning usually ends with ..........
questions.explanation: The .edu ending is used only by accredited post-secondary institutions, so D is correct. The other endings are open to wider groups: .com (A) can be bought by anyone, .gov (B) belongs to government, and .org (C) is for organisations of any kind.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: The number generated when a library material is catalogued is called ...........
questions.explanation: The number generated when a material is catalogued is the call number, also known as the call mark, which you need to find the book on the shelf. So D is correct. Library number, book number and cataloguing number (A, B and C) are not the technical term used in the library.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Any information retrieved from the Internet can be considered accurate
questions.explanation: The statement is false: anyone with access can put false information online and there are no general rules on web accuracy, so information from the Internet must always be evaluated before you trust it (C). Options A, B and D all accept the claim in some form, which is risky.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Books on Sociology in the University of Lagos Library can be found in ........
questions.explanation: The University of Lagos main library uses the Library of Congress scheme, where class H is Social Science and the sub-class HM is Sociology (General), so B is correct. HC is Economic History and Conditions, which makes D wrong, and TA and NA fall under Technology and Fine Art, not the social sciences.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: The acronym 'OPAC' means ................
questions.explanation: OPAC stands for Online Public Access Catalogue, the electronic version of the library catalogue, which can be searched by title, author, series and keywords. Options A and C change 'Public' to 'primary' or 'private', which is wrong because the catalogue is open to all library users.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: One can search the library catalogue for information materials using all EXCEPT .........
questions.explanation: The manual catalogue is searched by author, title and subject, and the OPAC adds series and keywords. Language is not an access point of the library catalogue, so A is the odd one out, while B, C and D are standard ways of searching.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: The Classification Scheme used for classifying and arranging library books in the University of Lagos Library is:
questions.explanation: The University of Lagos main library arranges its items by the Library of Congress (LC) classification scheme, which uses the letters A to Z for the main classes (C). Options A and B are not real schemes, and D, cataloguing and classification, describes the general activity rather than a named scheme.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: The College of Medicine Library, Idi-Araba, classifies its books using the
questions.explanation: The College of Medicine Library at Idi-Araba uses the National Library of Medicine scheme, which is designed for the medical sciences. The Library of Congress scheme is the tempting choice because the UNILAG main library uses it, but the medical library follows NLM.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: The two public catalogue cabinets in the UNILAG library are the
questions.explanation: UNILAG has two public catalogue cabinets: one for Author/Title and one for Subject. The Shelf-list and Authority catalogues also exist, but they are for official (staff) use, not for the public.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Which catalogues in the library are meant for official use rather than for library users?

options.a: The card catalogue and the OPAC

questions.explanation: The Shelf-list and the Authority catalogues are kept for official use by library staff. The Author/Title and Subject catalogues are the tempting wrong answer, but those are the two public cabinets that users consult.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Indexes and abstracts are often described as
questions.explanation: Indexes and abstracts are called bridges to published information because they lead the user to articles and documents that have been published. They are not official-use catalogues; that term refers to the Shelf-list and Authority catalogues kept by library staff.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Which of the following best describes an index?

options.a: A pointer that gives entry points to information but not the full text
options.b: A brief summary of a book, article or thesis
options.c: The number that shows where a book is shelved
options.d: A list of books or written works on a subject

questions.explanation: An index is a pointer or indicator: it tells you where information can be found but does not give you the full text. A brief summary of a book or article is an abstract, which is a different tool, even though the two are often mentioned together.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: Engineering Index and Index Medicus are examples of
questions.explanation: Engineering Index, Index Medicus and the Newspaper Index are all indexes, which point to where information can be found. They are not abstracts; examples of abstracts are Chemical Abstracts, Dissertation Abstracts and LISA, which give brief summaries of documents.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: NBN and BNB are examples of which information retrieval tool?
questions.explanation: A bibliography is a list of books or other written works on a subject, and NBN and BNB are examples of such lists. Indexes are tempting because they also point to information, but examples of indexes are Engineering Index and Index Medicus.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: In a library catalogue, terms that lead the user from known terms to unknown ones and back are called
questions.explanation: Cross-references link related terms in the catalogue, taking the user from a term they know to one they do not know, and back. A call number is different: it is the number generated when an item is catalogued and shows where it is located.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: A UNILAG student searching the OPAC with "Author (last name first)" for a book by Chinua Achebe should type
questions.explanation: An author search with "last name first" requires the form LAST NAME, FIRST NAME, so the entry is "Achebe, Chinua". "Chinua Achebe" is how the name is normally written, which makes it tempting, but it puts the first name first.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: A law student at UNILAG wants databases devoted to legal information. Which group should she use?
questions.explanation: Westlaw, HeinOnline and LexisNexis are the law databases. EBSCOhost and JSTOR are tempting because they are well known, but they are interdisciplinary databases covering many subjects, not law specifically.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: When results in a library database are ranked by date, they are arranged

options.a: chronologically, on a first in, first out basis
options.b: chronologically, on a last in, first out basis
options.d: by how often the search terms appear

questions.explanation: Ranking by date is chronological and follows LIFO, last in, first out, so the newest items appear first. Ranking by how often the search terms appear is a different method, ranking by relevance.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: In the Library of Congress scheme, books on Mathematics are found in subclass
questions.explanation: Under class Q (Science), QA is Mathematics. QC is Physics and QD is Chemistry, and HA, though it holds Statistics, belongs to the Social science class H.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: A Business Administration student at UNILAG wants books on finance. Under the Library of Congress scheme, she should go to subclass
questions.explanation: Under class H (Social science), HG is Finance. HF is the closest wrong choice, but it holds Commerce, while HB is Economic theory and HC is Economic history.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: In the National Library of Medicine (NLM) scheme, the preclinical sciences are classed in
questions.explanation: NLM places the preclinical sciences, such as Human Anatomy (QS) and Physiology (QT), in QS to QZ. W to WZ is the tempting choice, but that range is used for medicine itself, such as WY Nursing.

questions.topic: Information Retrieval Tools
questions.question: A UNILAG student needs a book held only by another university's library. Since students do not have reciprocal borrowing rights at all Nigerian universities, the service to use is
questions.explanation: Interlibrary loan lets UNILAG obtain an item from another library for its user, although it can take a week or more. An OPAC advanced search is tempting, but it only searches the library's own catalogue and cannot bring in a book from elsewhere.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Meta Search involves use of ........................
questions.explanation: A meta search uses meta search engines, option A, such as Dogpile, Metacrawler, Search.com and Vivisimo, which send your query to several ordinary search engines at once and gather the results together. Options B, C and D (primary, advanced or basic search engines) describe single search engines or search modes, not the tool that performs a meta search.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: A quote is used in research write up to..................
questions.explanation: You use a quotation to add the power of the author's own words to support your argument, and also to disagree with an author, compare points of view or note existing research, so D is correct. Showing off your writing skills, using vocabulary or convincing your supervisor (A, B and C) are not academic reasons for quoting.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: "OR" is used as a search strategy when a user wants to ........... the search
questions.explanation: The Boolean operator OR connects similar concepts or synonyms and broadens your search, because it tells the database that any of the terms may be present. Options A and D (limit, narrow) describe what AND and NOT do, and B (develop) is not a search function.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: .............. is done to reduce the amount of items retrieved in advanced search
questions.explanation: Filtering is what you do in an advanced search to refine for relevancy and reduce the number of items retrieved, using multiple search fields. Option D (simple search) does the opposite, often returning a huge amount of output, and B and C (exercises, research) are not search operations.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Subject Searching allows one to ...........

options.c: Browse for items by clause heading
options.d: Browse for items by phrase heading

questions.explanation: A subject search lets you browse for items by subject heading, returning only records where the term appears in the subject field. Option A is too general, since the OPAC can also be searched by title, author, series or keyword, and C and D name search types that do not exist.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: A useful search tool for academic information is ..............
questions.explanation: Google Scholar is a useful search tool for academic information because it indexes scholarly materials such as books, patents, journal articles and conference papers. Option D (Google) is tempting, but ordinary Google searches the whole web with no selection for scholarly quality. A (web crawler) is a program that collects web pages and B (Opera Mini) is a browser, not a search tool.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Advanced search allows you to limit your searches by:
questions.explanation: Advanced or field searching lets you narrow a search by specific fields such as year of publication, language or author, so B is correct. Size, number of pages and volume (A, C and D) are not standard limiters in library databases.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: When keywords are embedded in quotes, the type of search performed is ..............
questions.explanation: Phrase searching puts the keywords in quotation marks so the search engine returns only records where those words appear side by side in that order. Option C (Boolean search) uses operators like AND and OR, and B (subject search) searches the subject field, so neither depends on quotation marks.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: ............. allows a User to apply multiple search fields
questions.explanation: Advanced search lets the user apply multiple search fields and filters to narrow down results. Options B and D (quick and simple search) use a single keyword box, and A (complex search) is not a recognised search type.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: All of these are the advantages of using advanced search EXCEPT ...........

options.b: Ability to reduce number of items retrieved
options.c: Ability to use multiple search fields
options.d: Ability to retrieve huge amount of information

questions.explanation: The advantages of advanced search are that you can apply filters, reduce the number of items retrieved and use multiple search fields. Retrieving a huge amount of information is what a simple search tends to do, not an advantage of advanced search, so D is the exception.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: When there are too few sources retrieved for a search, one can ............

options.b: Combine synonymous terms with the OR Boolean operator

questions.explanation: When too few sources come back, you should broaden the search by combining synonymous terms with the OR operator. Options A and C (AND and NOT) do the opposite, since both narrow a search and are used when there are too many results.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: The use of keywords to perform quick information search is known as ............
questions.explanation: A simple search uses a few keywords to carry out a quick information search in a database or search engine. Option D (advanced search) involves filters and multiple fields, and C (meta search) uses several search engines at once, so neither is the quick keyword search described. Option B is not a recognised type.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Effective use of the library resources requires ...............
questions.explanation: Effective use of library resources requires search strategies, which is the art of planning and conducting searches to get the most efficient result. Punctuality, smartness and maturity (A, C and D) are personal qualities that do not by themselves help you find information.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: The Boolean operator "OR" is used in a search to .............
questions.explanation: OR connects two or more similar concepts or synonyms and broadens a search, because any one of the terms can appear in the results. Option D describes NOT, which excludes words, and A does not describe any Boolean operator.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: A research exercise must be ..............driven
questions.explanation: A research exercise must be driven by a subject or topic, because identifying the subject matter is the first step in a search strategy. Option A, strategy, is the overall plan built around the topic, and B and D are not terms used in this context.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Any of these can be used as method of saving information materials retrieved from an electronic source EXCEPT \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

options.b: Save the citation information/full text article

questions.explanation: Memorising a source leaves you no record to return to, so it is not a way of saving retrieved information (C). Catalogues and databases let you email, print or save the citation information and often the full text of an article, which is why A, B and D are all valid, and keeping a back-up copy is wise.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: The following are search techniques EXCEPT..............
questions.explanation: Filtering is not a search technique in its own right; it is something advanced searching does to reduce the number of items retrieved (D). The recognised search techniques are Boolean searching, parenthesis, phrase searching, truncation, wildcards and field searching, which is why A, B and C are not the exception.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: When you retrieve research results that are too broad or unrelated, the way out is to...........
questions.explanation: When your results are too broad or unrelated, you need to rethink your search strategy, for example by adding AND terms, using phrase searching or choosing more specific vocabulary (A). Changing your topic (B) abandons the research rather than improving the search, and changing the author or your location (C and D) would not make the results more relevant.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: What is the process employed in achieving effective search results?
questions.explanation: Search strategy is the art of planning and conducting searches to get the most efficient result, so it is the process asked about (B). Key (A) and concept (D) are elements you use within a search, while a call number (C) is the shelf address of a book, not a process.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: When a user deploys a variety of search tools simultaneously, it is called ........
questions.explanation: A meta search is one where the user uses a variety of search tools at the same time, through meta search engines such as Dogpile and Metacrawler that search Google, Yahoo and others at once (A). Advanced search (B) applies filters and multiple fields within one tool, and simple search (C) uses a few keywords in a single search box.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: The asterisk sign (\*) in a search is known as .............
questions.explanation: Truncation means putting an asterisk (*) after the root of a word so the search retrieves all its variations, for example teen* finding teens and teenagers (D). Option B, wildcard, is tempting, but wildcards replace a single letter and most commonly use the ? symbol, as in colo?r. Phrase searching (C) uses quotation marks, and simple search (A) is a basic keyword search.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: In a basic search strategy, a general overview of a topic is best obtained from

options.b: a general encyclopaedia such as Britannica or Americana

questions.explanation: After identifying the topic, the second step is to get a general overview, for example from a general encyclopaedia such as Britannica or Americana. Abstracts and indexes are tempting, but they belong to the third step, the narrower overview.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct order of the three basic steps in a search strategy?

options.a: Identify the topic, take a narrower overview, get a general overview
options.b: Get a general overview, identify the topic, take a narrower overview
options.c: Identify the topic, get a general overview, take a narrower overview
options.d: Take a narrower overview, get a general overview, identify the topic

questions.explanation: A search begins by identifying the subject or topic, then moves to a general overview, and ends with a narrower overview using abstracts, indexes, bibliographies or the catalogue. Starting with the general overview is tempting, but a research exercise must be topic-driven, so the topic comes first.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: In the five stages of electronic searching, what is the final stage?
questions.explanation: The five stages end with reviewing the results and refining the search. Running the search is tempting, but it is the fourth stage; after it you still review what you found and adjust.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: In the five stages of electronic searching, which stage comes immediately after "Decide which resources to use"?

options.a: Find out what search options they offer

questions.explanation: Once you have chosen your resources, the next stage is to find out what search options they offer, and only then do you run the search. "Run the search" is tempting, but it is the fourth stage, not the third.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Boolean searching is based on the symbolic logic developed by
questions.explanation: Boolean searching takes its name from George Boole, a 19th-century English mathematician whose symbolic logic underlies the AND, OR and NOT operators. The option describing him as a 20th-century American librarian gets the name right but his century, nationality and profession wrong.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: What is the effect of using AND between search terms?

options.a: It excludes the second term from the results
options.b: It makes the terms appear side by side as a phrase
options.c: It broadens the search, because any of the terms may appear
options.d: It narrows the search, because all the terms must appear

questions.explanation: AND narrows a search because every record retrieved must contain all the terms. Broadening, where any of the terms may appear, is what OR does, so that option is the most tempting mix-up.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: A student searches for "cloning NOT sheep". What will the results contain?

options.a: Records on sheep that do not mention cloning
options.b: Records on cloning that do not mention sheep
options.c: Records on both cloning and sheep
options.d: Records on either cloning or sheep

questions.explanation: NOT excludes the term that follows it, so the search keeps records on cloning and removes any that mention sheep. Records on both cloning and sheep would come from AND, which is the most likely confusion.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: When you type several words into Google without any operator between them, Google treats them as if they were joined by
questions.explanation: Google implies AND between the terms you type, so it looks for pages containing all of them. It does not assume quotation marks; without them the words do not have to appear side by side as a phrase.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: In the search "(vomit OR diarrhoea) AND blood", why are vomit OR diarrhoea placed in parentheses?

options.a: So that those terms are excluded from the search
options.b: So that the search ignores different word endings
options.c: So that the two words must appear side by side
options.d: So that the terms inside the parentheses are read first

questions.explanation: Terms inside parentheses are read first, so the search first gathers records on vomit or diarrhoea and then keeps those that also mention blood. Making words appear side by side is the job of quotation marks in phrase searching, not parentheses.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Which of the following search techniques broadens a search?
questions.explanation: Truncation broadens a search because a root with an asterisk retrieves all its endings, such as teen, teens and teenager. Phrase searching is tempting because it also uses a symbol, but quotation marks force the words to appear side by side, which narrows the search.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: A search for "colo?r" that retrieves both "color" and "colour" is using
questions.explanation: A wildcard, usually "?", stands for one character, which makes it useful for US and UK spellings such as color and colour. Truncation is the closest wrong answer, but it uses an asterisk at the end of a root to pick up all possible endings.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: A student in Ikeja limits a search so that her keyword must appear in the title and the results must be PDF files. Which technique is she using?
questions.explanation: Field searching restricts the search to a specific part of the record, such as the title, author, date range, language, domain or file type. Boolean searching is tempting, but it combines terms with AND, OR and NOT rather than targeting parts of the record.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Which type of searching uses controlled vocabulary and searches only the subject or descriptor field?
questions.explanation: Subject searching relies on fixed subject headings (controlled vocabulary) and looks only in the subject or descriptor field, which makes it less flexible but gives very relevant results. Keyword searching is the opposite: it matches natural-language words anywhere in the record.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Search engines build their huge databases of Internet files by using

options.a: librarians who select and evaluate each file

questions.explanation: Search engines collect Internet files automatically with programs called crawlers, robots or spiders. Librarians who select and evaluate each file is the tempting wrong option, but search engines have no selection or evaluation policy at all.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Which of the following statements about search engines such as Google is true?

options.a: They have no selection or evaluation policy
options.b: They index only peer-reviewed journal articles
options.c: They search only the subject or descriptor field
options.d: They are subscribed to by the university library

questions.explanation: Search engines collect whatever their crawlers find and have no selection or evaluation policy, which is why their results must be judged carefully. Being subscribed to by the library describes library databases such as JSTOR and EBSCOhost, not search engines.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: Which of the following is a meta search engine?
questions.explanation: Dogpile, like Search.com and Metacrawler, is a meta search engine that searches several tools such as Google and Yahoo at the same time. JSTOR and EBSCOhost are library databases, and Google Scholar is a single search tool for academic information.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: A 100L student researching "the effects of acid rain on the crops in Ogun State" should prepare keywords by

options.a: keeping only the verbs in the sentence
options.b: typing the full sentence exactly as written
options.c: using nouns and noun phrases and dropping articles and prepositions
options.d: putting the whole sentence in quotation marks

questions.explanation: Good keywords are nouns and noun phrases, such as acid rain, crops and Ogun State, with words like "the" and "on" left out. Typing the full sentence is tempting, but searches work poorly with full sentences because the extra words add nothing useful.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: A search returns too many unrelated results. Which of the following would help?
questions.explanation: Restricting the search to the title field narrows the results, as do AND, NOT, phrase searching and more specific vocabulary. Combining synonyms with OR is the most tempting wrong option, but it broadens a search and is the remedy for too few results.

questions.topic: Search Strategies
questions.question: A simple search is most suitable when

options.a: you need to filter results by year of publication
options.b: you are unsure of what you need or the topic is unfocused
options.c: you want to use many search tools at the same time
options.d: you want to apply several search fields at once

questions.explanation: A simple search is a quick keyword search that suits an unfocused topic such as "Malaria and Africa", although it brings back a huge, often irrelevant output. Filtering by year of publication and applying several search fields are features of advanced search.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: If a scholar does not acknowledge all quoted and borrowed ideas as he reads and writes, he is guilty of
questions.explanation: Plagiarism is using someone's work or ideas without permission or without acknowledging where it came from, and it is often called academic theft, so B is correct. A scholar who does not acknowledge quoted and borrowed ideas is guilty of it. Perjury (A) is lying under oath, and permutation (C) and permissiveness (D) have nothing to do with academic honesty.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: A full entry in a bibliography must show:

options.b: Title of work & place of publication

questions.explanation: A full bibliography entry must identify the work completely, so it gives the author's name and year of publication, the title of the work, the place of publication and the publisher. Each of A, B and C is only part of a complete entry, so D, all of the above, is correct.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: The arrangement of bibliography is
questions.explanation: A bibliography is arranged alphabetically, option C, using the author's surname (or the title if there is no author), so readers can find any source quickly. Chronological order (A) is not the standard, and idiosyncratic (B) or whimsical (D) arrangements would make the list useless to readers.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: The bibliography is usually located at ___ part of a research work
questions.explanation: The bibliography, or reference list, is placed at the end of a research work, option C, so readers can follow the brief in-text citations to the full details of each source. The beginning (A) and preliminary pages (D) hold items like the title page and abstract, and nothing like a bibliography goes in the middle (B).

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: All of the following sources can be cited in a reference list EXCEPT.........

options.a: Chapter or article in edited book

questions.explanation: Books, chapters or articles in edited books, and web pages can all be cited in a reference list, so every source in A, B and C is allowed. Since none of them is excluded, D, none of the above, is correct. Choosing A, B or C would wrongly suggest that a legitimate source type cannot be referenced.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: In-text citation appears in the body of the manuscript.
questions.explanation: The statement is true, option C. Referencing has two parts: the in-text citation, which appears in the body of the manuscript right where another writer's idea or words are used, and the reference list at the end of the work. Options A, B and D wrongly suggest the in-text citation sits somewhere other than the manuscript.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Copyrighted works are protected by .............
questions.explanation: Copyright law (or author's right) says that no one may use a creative work without the owner's permission, and anyone who does so is liable to prosecution, so B, law, is correct. The author (C) owns the right, but the protection comes from the law, while a book seller (A) and a publisher (D) merely sell or produce the work.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: A student that has committed plagiarism can be ...........
questions.explanation: A student caught plagiarising can be suspended or rusticated, meaning sent away from school for a period, so A is correct. Option B, jailed, is tempting because prosecution is possible, but the usual penalty for a student is suspension or rustication. Options C and D (an award, a promotion) are rewards, not punishments.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: To avoid plagiarism

options.a: Other people's ideas must be paraphrased and cited

questions.explanation: Plagiarism is avoided by acknowledging the work you use: paraphrasing other people's ideas properly and citing the sources in the prescribed style and the reference list. Option A captures exactly that. Consulting a lecturer (B), using the library (C) or reading the manuscript (D) may be good habits, but none of them by itself stops you from plagiarising.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: One of these does not appear in the reference list
questions.explanation: A reference list entry records the author's surname and initials, the title of the work, and publication details such as place, publisher, date and page numbers. A keyword is just a term you type into a search engine or database to find material, so it never appears in a reference entry. That makes D correct, while A, B and C are all standard parts of a reference.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: All are eligible for copyright according to World Intellectual Property Organization, EXCEPT ........
questions.explanation: Works eligible for copyright under the World Intellectual Property Organization include books, music, paintings, sculpture, films, computer programs, databases, advertisements, maps and technical drawings. Complimentary cards are not on that list, so D is the exception, while A, B and C are all eligible.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Fair use allows the usage of copyrighted works for ............
questions.explanation: Fair use allows copyrighted works to be used without permission for purposes such as criticism, comment, news reporting and teaching, in short for academic purposes within certain limits. Options A and C (business, publishing) are commercial uses that need permission, and B (prosecution) is what can happen when copyright is infringed, not a permitted use.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: The most commonly used citation style in Social sciences is ..............
questions.explanation: APA (American Psychological Association) style is the one most commonly used to cite sources in the social sciences. Option B (MLA) is associated with composition and language courses, D (Chicago) with the humanities, and C (Harvard) is an author-date style popular with university students generally but not tied to the social sciences.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: To avoid plagiarism, all used works must be ........
questions.explanation: To avoid plagiarism, any work you use must be cited, through proper in-text citation and a reference list, so the original author gets credit. Typing, noting or grouping the works (B, C and D) does not credit the author and so does not prevent plagiarism.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: APA recommends that a book without an author should be cited in the text using .........

options.c: The first few words of the title

questions.explanation: When a book has no author, APA uses the first few words of the title in place of the author's name in the in-text citation, followed by the year. Option A is wrong because the year alone cannot tell the reader which source is meant, and B and D (publisher, library) are never used in place of the author.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: ............ is when a researcher paraphrases correctly
questions.explanation: Fair use allows copyrighted material to be used for academic purposes within limits, and paraphrasing correctly, with acknowledgment, is one of the skills that keeps a researcher within it. Option C (plagiarism) is using someone's work without acknowledgment, and A (unfair use) is copying indiscriminately, so correct paraphrasing is the opposite of both. Option B is not the term used.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: An offence of self-plagiarism is said to have been committed if ..........

options.b: You copy from your previous assignment for a new assignment without acknowledgment
options.c: You copy from your lecturer's handout without acknowledgement
options.d: You copy from the internet without acknowledgement

questions.explanation: Self-plagiarism happens when you copy from your own previous assignment for a new one without acknowledgment, because even your own earlier work must be cited. Options C and D describe ordinary plagiarism of other people's material, since the handout and the internet content are not your own work. Option A is wrong because B fits.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Bibliography refers to...................

options.b: A list of the written sources of information on a subject
options.c: A list of books and articles that have been used by someone when writing on a subject
options.d: List of books, magazines, articles, etc. about a particular subject

questions.explanation: A bibliography is a list of written sources of information on a subject, including the books and articles consulted while preparing a piece of work. Because B, C and D each express part of that definition, 'All of these' (A) is the best answer.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: ............. is the act of using copyrighted work without permission or acknowledging the source.
questions.explanation: Plagiarism is using someone's work without permission or without acknowledging the source, and it is often described as academic theft. Copying and pasting, and copying (B and D) are actions that can lead to plagiarism but are not the name of the offence, and dubbing (A) means adding a new soundtrack to a film.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Which of the reference style excludes the year of publication in the in-text citation?
questions.explanation: In MLA style, the in-text citation gives the author's last name and the page number, for example (McDonagh 80), with no year. APA and Harvard (B and D) are author-date styles that include the year, and MPA (C) is not a referencing style.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Referencing is composed of two parts namely...................
questions.explanation: Referencing has two parts: in-text referencing, which is the brief citation in the body of your work, and the reference list at the end, which gives the full details. So A is correct. Options B, C and D use labels that do not exist in any referencing style.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: All of these are referencing styles EXCEPT ............
questions.explanation: APA, MLA, Harvard and Chicago are the main referencing styles, so A, C and D are all real styles. NLA is not a referencing style, which makes B the exception.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: When you paraphrase a quote,

options.c: you reuse it in another language

questions.explanation: To paraphrase is to express another writer's ideas in your own words. Options B and D describe quoting verbatim, which is the opposite of paraphrasing, and C, reusing it in another language, is translation, not paraphrase.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: When using the American Psychological Association (APA) referencing style, the reference list should be arranged in ....... order
questions.explanation: An APA reference list is set out in alphabetical order, using the author's surname, or the title when there is no author. Chronological order (B) is wrong because the date comes after the author, not first. Numerical order (A) belongs to numbered styles, not APA, and citation order (D) is not an APA rule.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Citation is a skill that must be learnt ...........
questions.explanation: Citation is a skill students must learn for academic purposes: to avoid plagiarism in an academic setting you must paraphrase correctly and acknowledge every source you use (D). Options A and B describe library skills rather than the reason for citing, and chatting online (C) has nothing to do with acknowledging sources.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: The punishment for violating copyright law is ..............

options.a: Prosecute the offender under the law
options.c: Ban the offender from the library

questions.explanation: Copyrighted works are protected by law, so anyone who violates copyright can be prosecuted under the law (A). 'All of the above' (B) cannot be right because it would include killing the offender (D), which is not a legal punishment. A library ban (C) is not the legal penalty for breaking copyright law.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Using the APA referencing style, any article retrieved from a website with no date of publication should be cited in the reference list but the following information must be included:

options.a: The url from where the article was accessed
options.b: The date the article was retrieved
options.c: The date and URL from where the document was obtained

questions.explanation: An APA reference for a web document with no date uses (n.d.) and then states when and where it was obtained, as in 'Retrieved October 17, 2008, from' followed by the URL, so both the retrieval date and the URL are needed (C). Options A and B each give only one of the two required pieces of information, so they are incomplete.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: The word "plagiarism" comes from the Latin word plagiarius, which means
questions.explanation: Plagiarism comes from the Latin plagiarius, meaning "kidnapper", because the plagiarist carries off someone else's work as if it were his own. "Thief of books" is tempting since plagiarism is called academic theft, but that is not the meaning of the Latin word.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Using the Internet to take another person's ideas or expression without acknowledgement is known as
questions.explanation: Cyber plagiarism is plagiarism carried out through the Internet, such as copying text from a website. Self-plagiarism is tempting, but it means copying from your own earlier assignment for a new one without acknowledgement.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Using APA style, which of the following is cited in the text but NOT included in the reference list?

options.a: A journal article read in JSTOR
options.b: A telephone conversation with a bank manager in Lagos
options.d: A government report found on a website

questions.explanation: Personal communications such as conversations and emails cannot be retrieved by the reader, so they are cited only in the text. A government report on a website is tempting, but it can be retrieved, so it appears in both the text and the reference list.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: In APA style, a direct quotation of 40 words or more should be

options.a: placed within the text in single quotation marks and italics
options.b: moved to a footnote at the bottom of the page
options.c: placed within the text in double quotation marks
options.d: set as a block on a new line, indented, without quotation marks

questions.explanation: A quotation of 40 words or more is set as a block starting on a new line, indented 5 spaces, with no quotation marks. Putting it in the text within double quotation marks is the rule for quotations of fewer than 40 words, which is why that option is tempting.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: A student read Talbot and Verrinder (2005), who quote Palfrey (2000), but she never read Palfrey's own work. In APA style, which work goes in her reference list?

options.b: Both Palfrey (2000) and Talbot and Verrinder (2005)

questions.explanation: In a secondary citation, only the work you actually read goes in the reference list, so Talbot and Verrinder is listed and Palfrey is mentioned in the text as "as cited in". Listing both is tempting, but Palfrey's work was not consulted directly.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Which of the following is a correctly formatted Harvard in-text citation?
questions.explanation: Harvard is an author-date style with no comma between the author and the year, as in (Austen 1813, p. 64). The version with a comma after Austen looks very similar, but that comma is the APA pattern, while (Austen 64) is the MLA author-page form.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Which of the following is an entry in MLA Works Cited format?

options.a: McDonagh, Sean. Why are we Deaf to the Cry of the Earth. Dublin: Veritas, 2001.
options.b: McDonagh, S. (2001). Why are we deaf to the cry of the earth. Dublin: Veritas.
options.c: Sean McDonagh, 2001. Dublin: Veritas. Why are we Deaf to the Cry of the Earth.
options.d: McDonagh, S 2001, Why are we deaf to the cry of the earth, Veritas, Dublin.

questions.explanation: MLA Works Cited entries follow the pattern Last name, First name. Title. Place: Publisher, Year, with the year at the end. The entry with "(2001)" straight after the initial is the APA pattern, and the one with the year after the name and no brackets is Harvard.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: In the APA reference "Australian Nursing Journal, 12(7), 23-25", which part is italicised along with the journal title?

options.b: Both the volume and the issue numbers

questions.explanation: In APA, the journal title and its volume number are italicised, while the issue number in brackets is not. Italicising both the volume and issue numbers is the tempting mistake, because they sit side by side.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a purpose allowed under fair use?

options.b: Selling photocopies of a published book for profit

questions.explanation: Fair use permits criticism, comment, news reporting, teaching and similar non-commercial uses of copyrighted works. Selling photocopies for profit is commercial, so it falls outside fair use; teaching may look like it needs permission, but it is one of the allowed purposes.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: Copying a copyrighted work indiscriminately, with or without acknowledgement, is called
questions.explanation: Unfair use is indiscriminate copying of a copyrighted work, and acknowledging the author does not make it acceptable. Fair use is the tempting opposite: it is use for academic and similar purposes up to a certain limit.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: A member of staff found guilty of plagiarism can face
questions.explanation: For staff, the consequence of plagiarism is summary dismissal, and prosecution is also possible. Rustication is tempting, but it is a penalty for students, together with suspension.

questions.topic: Style Manual: Citation and Referencing
questions.question: In APA style, page numbers are NOT required in the in-text citation when you

options.b: paraphrase or summarise an author's idea
options.c: quote 40 words or more as a block
options.d: quote a definition word for word

questions.explanation: A paraphrase or summary needs only the author's surname and the year, with no page number. Any direct quotation, short or long, needs the page number as well, which rules out the other three options.
